answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create a time-constrained decision. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor has delivered reliable onboarding and accurate operations previously. However, the assembly line operates at 94% committed volume with zero buffer—any supply interruption directly cascades to production commitments. Switching to the low-cost vendor alone meets the financial mandate but eliminates redundancy. The decision balances: (1) verified low-cost vendor capability from c2; (2) rejected multi-year incumbent commitment upside from c6 due to budget pressure; (3) rejected renegotiation path from c4 as unlikely to yield 18% savings in 14 days. The standard_experiment scale allows phased volume migration to the low-cost vendor while keeping incumbent relationship warm for 60–90 days as contingency. This preserves optionality if supply instability emerges, though it does not eliminate the single-point-of-failure risk that memory_c3 specifically warned against. The constraint is real: one decision only, expiring contract, zero budget buffer for a second-source split. Switching meets the mandate; deferring is not viable given the no-auto-renew clause.
